Verse Engine 2.7: what's new for you#

Verse Engine 2.7 is live. The changelog lists every change; this is the short version, written for the people who send links to clients rather than the people who build the engine. Eight things are new. Each one has a short guide, linked below.

Realistic lighting, automatically#

Until now a model looked its best when a designer had "baked" the lighting into it first, in Blender or another 3D tool. If you upload a raw model, the upload card now shows a Lighting choice. Pick Bake for me (preview or final; Keep as exported is the default) and the cloud adds soft shadows and light before the link is ready. No extra software, no second upload. Guide: Bake for me.

Photo-quality stills#

Stand still in any scene and, within a second or two, the view turns into a photo-quality image: soft reflections, light bouncing off walls, glass that looks like glass. Move and it goes back to the fast, walkable view. You can also change every lamp and the sun's position right from the link. Guide: Tune quality.

Open BIM files#

Architects and developers can upload an IFC or USD file straight from their BIM tool. Every wall, door and fixture stays its own object: click one to see its details, hide or isolate it, or search the model floor by floor. Guide: Publish from IFC.

See it in your room#

A chair, a lamp, a product: anything at household scale opens in phone AR with one tap, on Android and iPhone, with no app to install. The same link works on a laptop as a normal 3D view. Guide: View in AR.

Present together#

Open a scene with your client and talk inside it. One person presents and everyone follows their view; you can point things out, take questions, and hand over to a colleague mid-tour. Guide: Present a scene.

Options and prices#

Let clients switch finishes, fabrics and variants inside the link, with SKUs and prices shown as they choose. Every choice can be sent to your own system, so an order or a quote starts from what the client actually picked. Guide: Build a configurator.

Screens and sound#

TVs and screens in a scene can play video, and sound comes from where it should: a television in the living room is louder in the living room. Guide: Video and audio.

Outdoors#

Exteriors get a real sky that lights the scene, rain or snow, fog, and ground you can walk on. Good for a township, a villa plot or a storefront seen from the street. Guide: Exteriors.

And on every device#

Behind all of this is a built-in autopilot that adjusts sharpness and effects many times a second, so the same link stays smooth from a budget Android phone to a high-end laptop, and eases off before a phone gets hot. The link opens in seconds; the first picture is a soft version of the whole space, which then sharpens wherever you look.

If you were already using Verse#

Nothing you have shared changes. Existing links keep working and keep their look. New uploads get the Lighting choice on the upload card; everything else is on by default or a tick away in the viewer.

Try it at the app, or read the five-minute guide.
